question.leadin: Pope Sixtus V supported this fleet that was defeated with the help of the "Protestant Wind"
question.text: Name this royal navy sent by Philip II in 1588 to invade England and restore Catholicism.
question.answerHtml: Spanish Armada [or la Grande y Felicísma Armada, or the Great and Most Fortunate Navy]
question.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Zaragoza increased the scope of this treaty in 1529.
swap.text: Name this treaty that created a line of demarcation 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, allowing Portugal to colonize the land east of the line and Spain the land to the west.
swap.clue: This treaty established a line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, which was later extended through both poles by the Treaty of Zaragoza.

question.text: The Duke of Wellington also led troops during the Peninsular War, a war over control of this location. This region contains Spain and Portugal, and is separated from France by the Pyrenees.
question.clue: The knight El Cid fought on both sides of a series of military campaigns in this region, which concluded in 1492 with the fall of the Emirate of Granada.

swap.text: Merged with the Carlists by Franco, this Spanish fascist movement was founded by Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera.
swap.clue: Two leaders of this party were buried within the Santa Cruz Basilica at the Valley of the Fallen.

question.leadin: This man was replaced in one post by Francisco de Bobadilla, who arrested him for slavery and corruption.
question.text: Name this Governor of the West Indies who committed a genocide against the Taino people. This founder of La Navidad was declared Admiral of the Ocean Sea.
question.clue: Historians have debated how accurate the only copy of this man's diary is to his actual views, as it comes down only via copies from an abstract made by the secretary of Bartolome de Las Casas.

swap.text: This Spanish king died before he could fulfill a promised audience to Las Casas. This leader of Aragon led Spain during the Reconquista with his wife Isabella.
swap.clue: He met with the Nasrid ruler Boabdil prior to besieging Granada, which he captured in 1492.

question.leadin: This man gained nationwide prestige after he crushed the Asturias miners' strike of 1934.
question.text: Name this man, who sent the Blue Division to fight for Nazi Germany on the Eastern Front during World War II. This dictator ruled his country under the title El Caudillo and came to prominence for his services in the Rif War.
question.clue: Since Luis Carrero Blanco was assassinated, this dictator picked Juan Carlos I to succeed him.

swap.text: Sephardic Jews were expelled from Castile and Aragon by this edict meant to prevent conversos from reverting to Judaism. This edict was formally revoked in 1968 following the Second Vatican Council.
swap.answerHtml: Alhambra Decree [accept Edict of Expulsion; accept Decreto de Alhambra or Edicto de Granada]
swap.clue: Ferdinand and Isabella passed this decree to expel the Jews from Spain, creating the Sephardic ("seh-FAR-dik") diaspora. This decree was partly reversed by Primo de Rivera, who allowed Sephardic Jews to claim Spanish citizenship.

question.text: Juana was the second daughter of this queen of Castile. Her marriage to Ferdinand of Aragon united the Spanish nation.
question.clue: This ruler was often advised by Tomas de Torquemada, who headed an institution set up by this monarch and her husband which often conducted auto-da-fe ceremonies.

swap.leadin: Give these terms from the rule of Napoleon.
swap.text: Known as War of Independence by native Spaniards, this attempt to subjugate Portugal and Spain lasted from 1808 to 1814.

question.leadin: Emilio Mola helped precipitate this event by declaring the pronuncimento.
question.text: Name this conflict between rebel groups like the Falange and the Second Republic under Manuel Azana, which ended with Francisco Franco establishing a dictatorship.
question.answerHtml: Spanish Civil War [prompt on partial answer; or guerra civil de Espana]
question.clue: Germany supported one side in this conflict with the Condor Legion.

swap.text: The first of the Spanish Bourbons was this grandson of Louis XIV. His accession in 1700 prompted the War of Spanish Succession, though he would stay in power until his death in 1746.
swap.clue: This king's opponents claimed that his reign was a violation of the Hague Partition Treaties.

question.leadin: A descendant of the Duchy of Vascony, its southern part was eventually absorbed by Castille.
question.text: Identify this kingdom spanning the Pyrenees ruled by kings like Sancho the Great, which had its capital at Pamplona and once shared its name with that city.
question.clue: Another ruler of this kingdom was offered the French crown by Etienne Marcel during the Jacquerie.

swap.text: This legendary Spanish warrior and Castilian national hero served Sancho II and later became the ruler of Valencia. He's memorialized by a lengthy "Cantar" [kahn-TAR], as well as a Pierre Corneille play.
swap.answerHtml: El Cid Campeador [or El Cid Campeador; or Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar; accept Le Cid; prompt on Díaz]
swap.clue: After his recall he fought off Tashafin's army, which had responded to pleas from local lords by forcing the Battle of az-Zallaqah, a massive Almoravid victory.

question.leadin: Name some things related to everyone's favorite medieval manuscript, the Liber feudorum maior.
question.text: The Liber feudorum maior was commissioned by Alfonso II from this state. Under Ferdinand II of this state, it combined with Castile, which was led by Isabella.
question.clue: A princess of this kingdom was the first woman named as an ambassador to another European nation, in this case England.

swap.leadin: Sebastian de Olmedo called him "the hammer of heretics, the light of Spain, the saviour of his country, the honour of his order."
swap.text: Name this Dominican monk who served as Spain's first Inquisitor General.
swap.clue: The co-rulers were also ardent supporters of the Inquisition, appointing this "hammer of heretics" as the brutal Grand Inquisitor.

question.text: An uprising known as the Zamacolada occurred after this Spanish prime minister tried to establish an independent port in Basque territory. This man became known as the "Prince of the Peace" after negotiating the Second Treaty of San Ildefonso in 1796.
question.answerHtml: Manuel de <u>Godoy</u> [or Manuel <u>Godoy</u> y Alvarez de Faria]
question.clue: He became his country's first commander to adopt the title of generalisimo while leading troops in the War of the Oranges.

swap.text: As an homage to Blanche, Louis IX gifted a moralizing Bible completed in this city to her nephew, Ferdinand III. A medieval "school of translators" in this Castilian city was instrumental in preserving Arabic scientific texts.
swap.answerHtml: Toledo [accept Toledo School of Translators or Escuela de Traductores de Toledo; accept Toledo Bible or Bible of Toledo]
swap.clue: The Spanish Nationalist newspaper was named for this city's Alcazar, which withstood a Republican siege.

question.text: This Spanish church doctor also railed against the Jews in On the Catholic Faith Against the Jews and maintained that the Earth was round in an encyclopedia entitled Etymologiae or Origins.
question.answerHtml: Saint Isidore of Seville [or San Isidro or San Isidoro de Sevilla; do NOT accept "San Isidro Labrador"]
question.clue: This man's younger sister Florentina allegedly held claim over forty convents, and at her request he wrote his two books Against the Jews, while his younger brother Fulgentius served as bishop of Astigi.

swap.leadin: Name these things about Muslim military failures on the Iberian Peninsula, FTP each.
swap.text: The decisive battle of the Reconquista proved to be this 1212 victory for a Christian force over the Almohad forces on the plains of Toledo. The Muslim defeat opened the heart of Andalucia to Christian advances.
swap.answer: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
swap.clue: A letter from one leader of this battle to Pope Innocent III details the capture of Baeza and Ubeda in its immediate aftermath.
